bull_bear.body: Strategy to divest non-core businesses (NODWIN, Sportskeeda, AdTech) and redeploy proceeds into core high-margin gaming; NODWIN planning independent fundraising of $100-200mn (primary/secondary) and IPO; Organic reinvestment in IP expansion and COE capabilities.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Regulatory delay in Bluetile acquisition (Spanish FDI); Google Core update impact on Sportskeeda traffic (revenue down 38% FY26); Seasonality in Fusebox titles; Integration risks with Bluetile; High amortization/write-offs in associates (NODWIN).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident and transformational; Emphasis on 'pivotal year', 'fundamental change', and 'operating leverage compounding'; Clear strategic clarity on focusing purely on gaming while monetizing non-core assets.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR 31cr 'other income' was a mark-to-market gain on Rusk Media investment, not cash flow; NODWIN's operational profitability is masked by a one-time INR 50cr goodwill write-off related to NH7 Weekender; AdTech revenue decline is a conscious strategic exit from low-margin traditional agency work to high-margin product-led DSP, not market loss.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The transaction was restructured from a phased deal (approximately 50% at closing for USD 100.3 million, earn-outs of up to USD 98.2 million, and a put/call over the remaining approximately 50% at 6.6x trailing CY EBITDA) to 100% at closing for a fixed USD 303 million all-cash - stated rationale: "Eliminated future valuation uncertainty", "Full economics from day one", "Immediate operating integration", "Simplified governance" and "Greater strategic flexibility".
- A newly constituted Investment Committee supervised the evaluation - reviewing the deal "against expected returns, downside risks, funding capacity and long-term shareholder value" - and will oversee consideration payments and material integration-related capital deployment; the Board retains final approval.
- The Investment Committee "will review and recommend all material future acquisitions, follow-on investments, divestments and other capital-allocation proposals", establishing a standing capital-allocation gate; its members are Muraarie Rajan (Independent Director), Mithun Padam Sacheti and Vivek Chopra (Non-Executive Directors).
- Growth capital is being routed into user acquisition and content rather than payout: UA scaled at Bluetile/BestPlay, Kiddopia and Fusebox with the deck acknowledging this "moderated near-term EBITDA".
- NODWIN "pressed pause on new acquisitions to fine-tune its M&A playbook" post-Freaks4u and, "Basis the refined M&A playbook, NODWIN is looking to restart its acquisition engine soon".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- brand: Animal Jam holds the top grossing position in its US app category — evidence: MD&A business table lists Animal Jam's market positioning as '#1 grossing app in its category in the US' (key market US ~90%)
- brand: Kiddopia ranks among the leading grossing kids' learning apps in the US — evidence: MD&A business table lists Kiddopia as 'Among the top 3 grossing apps in its category in the US' (key market US ~80%)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Platform dependence on Apple and Google — The company relies significantly on large third-party platforms for distribution and billing; changes in their policies, terms or web flows directly affect operations.
- Search-algorithm and traffic risk — Changes in platform search algorithms can cut traffic, revenue and EBITDA, as seen in Sportskeeda's US traffic decline after Google's March Core Update.
- Regulatory and policy risk — Government policy actions can affect operations and asset values, as the real-money-gaming ban did, leading to an impairment of the investment in Moonshine Technologies (PokerBaazi).
- Hit-driven performance variability — Gaming is hit-driven; businesses can become one-hit wonders or see high variability if a title fails to gain traction.
- Acquisition integration and new-IP incubation risk — An acquisition-led model carries integration risk and the risk of missing projected synergies; the company estimates a 70-80% failure rate for early-stage new-IP or micro-IP experiments.
- Seasonality tied to TV IP calendars — Revenue and EBITDA fluctuate significantly by quarter, particularly at Fusebox Games, whose titles are tied to the launch calendars of popular TV IPs.
- Geopolitical, macroeconomic and currency exposure — Global slowdowns (including Germany and wider Europe), Taiwan risk and US sanctions affect international operations such as Freaks 4U Gaming; currency gains and losses on international loans add earnings volatility.
- Stagnation in Western esports — Decline or stagnation of esports in Europe and the US can drive layoffs and business write-offs.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Framed as an evolution "from an entrepreneurial gaming company into a significantly larger and increasingly global gaming platform", with shared capabilities across user acquisition, data, product and growth "translating into stronger performance across the gaming portfolio".
- Gaming is the core: Q1FY27 gaming revenue of INR 275 Cr grew 14% YoY at a 19.5% EBITDA margin and "all gaming businesses remained EBITDA-positive".
- Post-consolidation the mix tilts decisively to gaming - "gaming represents approximately 84% of illustrative consolidated revenue" (deck's own illustrative arithmetic aggregation of Q1FY27 figures, expressly "not a forecast or pro forma financial statement").
- Bluetile is presented as an "AI-Powered Game Production Platform" where "One production platform behind every game" runs Block Blitz, Sort Journey, Hole Rush, Solitaire "...and 23 more live titles, all running on the same core".
- Fusebox "Ranks #1 in Free Apps and #5 in Top Grossing Apps Category in the US".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Leadership] Raymond A. Stauffer - Founder and former CEO of Bluetile and BestPlay - is appointed Chief Executive Officer of Nazara Technologies effective 1 September 2026, subject to relevant regulatory approvals, leading day-to-day Group operations, integration and shared operating capabilities; Nitish Mittersain continues as Founder and Managing Director shaping long-term strategy, portfolio direction and key relationships. Maxime Loppin is appointed CEO of Bluetile and BestPlay.
- [Deconsolidation] NODWIN has been deconsolidated from August 2025, which is why reported consolidated revenue declined 14% YoY while "Excluding NODWIN, comparable consolidated revenue grew approximately 9% YoY"; NODWIN now flows through share of loss from associates.
- [Reported loss] Q1FY27 reported PAT was a loss of INR 82 crore, which the deck attributes largely to share of loss from associates (INR 62 crore) and an impairment loss (INR 22 crore).
- [IPO readiness] NODWIN is described as having "Youth Media Strategy and IPO Readiness in Full Flow", with organic growth "poised to be at 30% for this FY"; its focus is stated as "Global South with offices across the world. Global North as revenue. Global South as execution".
- [Retention] NODWIN's ESOP plan is offered to all employees, "resulting in to sub-5% attrition", and founder retention post-earnouts has had "ZERO attritions"; NODWIN has also moved NH7 to a license model for India ("the license fee will go straight to the bottom line") and ended the MG deals for Comic Con in favour of direct ticket sales.

outlook.body: Bluetile acquisition (pending Spanish FDI approval, expected close in 3-4 weeks) adds INR 1,460cr revenue/INR 254cr EBITDA scale; AI-driven content generation reducing cost per unit; Potential divestment of NODWIN, Sportskeeda, and AdTech to unlock value; Expansion of Fusebox narrative IPs beyond 'Love Island'.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Gaming-first global platform: sharpen focus on core, high-margin IP-led gaming businesses; NODWIN was de-subsidiarised (associate from August 2025) as part of this portfolio restructuring.
- Deepen integration across the portfolio so shared functions and cross-group synergies are fully realised (Board priority #1).
- Drive operating leverage by scaling common infrastructure and the Centres of Excellence (user acquisition, data analytics, AI, growth, product) across all businesses (Board priority #2).
- Keep capital allocation disciplined and performance-linked while retaining flexibility to invest where it strengthens the platform; capital is deployed only where the CoE playbook can enhance execution (Board priority #3).
- Build an IP flywheel: turn successful titles into long-lived franchises with recurring monetisation through institutionalised LiveOps (Human: Fall Flat updates, Fusebox multi-IP narrative games, Monster High integration in Animal Jam, WCC4).
- Embed AI across the game lifecycle via a dedicated AI CoE (AI-assisted development of WCC4, AI moderation in Animal Jam, AI-native development capabilities from Bluetile).
- Build Nazara ID to establish direct relationships with Indian gamers and pursue cross-portfolio synergies through shared user-acquisition infrastructure.
- Inorganic growth centred on acquiring businesses with proven monetisation, distinctive IP and product-market fit; the company continues to evaluate acquisitions actively (proposed Bluetile Games and BestPlay acquisition is its largest ever).
- Extend IP reach to new platforms: Animal Jam on Roblox, Curve Games developing titles including Wobbly Life for Nintendo Switch 2.
- Expand offline experiential gaming: SMAAASH 2.0 relaunch with upgraded experiences and more IP integrations, and steady expansion of Funky Monkeys.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Nazara is asset-light; its expansion during FY 2025-26 came mainly through acquisitions and footprint growth rather than plant capex. It acquired 100% of Curve Digital Entertainment (PC/console publisher) through Nazara UK effective June 11, 2025; took 100% of Smaaash Entertainment under an NCLT-approved insolvency resolution plan effective June 06, 2025; bought the TJR/ITR Wrestling websites (May 2025) and PrimeTimer (July 2025) IP through Sportskeeda Inc.; NODWIN acquired AFK Gaming (July 2025); and Nazara Dubai subscribed to a minority CCPS stake in Getstan Technologies (STAN). Openplay was sold to associate Moonshine (May 2025) and NODWIN was de-subsidiarised to an associate (August 2025). Funky Monkeys expanded to 20 operational centres across key Indian cities under a playbook-led model. Looking ahead, management calls FY 2026-27 a year of integration, execution and scale: the proposed Bluetile Games (including BestPlay Systems) acquisition is to be fully integrated, SMAAASH is being stabilised ahead of a planned 'SMAAASH 2.0' relaunch, and the offline gaming portfolio is to expand steadily. Capex and R&D are described in BRSR as focused on technology capability, IT infrastructure, software and communication networks.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects FY 2026-27 to be a year of integration, execution and scale, built on full integration of Bluetile Games, maturation of the existing mobile portfolio and steady expansion of offline gaming.
- Mix shift toward high-margin, IP-led gaming is management's stated profitability driver, with gaming described as the dominant EBITDA contributor and more than 90% of gaming revenue coming from international markets.
- CoE-led operating leverage and user-acquisition efficiency are cited as the margin lever; integrating AI-driven capabilities and shared technology platforms is expected to unlock further efficiencies.
- India's shift away from real-money gaming (after the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025) toward skill-based, casual and mid-core formats is described as creating a more stable, investment-friendly environment.
- Structural industry tailwinds cited: wider smartphone and internet access, 5G rollout, growth of in-game advertising, localisation/vernacular content and cloud gaming.
- Kiddopia returned to subscriber growth, with management prioritising rebuilding subscriber momentum and planned higher user-acquisition spend over near-term monetisation.
- Curve Games is targeting a faster release cadence, with five to six new titles expected across FY 2026-27 and FY 2027-28; upcoming titles include Sovereign Tower, Dragon Shelter and Badlands Crew.
- Curve Games has secured an early foothold on Nintendo Switch 2 and is developing titles, including Wobbly Life, for it.
- WCC4 is being developed with AI-assisted coding, content creation and QA as part of expanding the WCC franchise.
- Fusebox Games launched two new IP-based narrative-style games on its existing engine, moving from single-IP to multi-IP.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Nazara fundamentally reshaped its profile in FY26 with gaming EBITDA contribution jumping to 90% and margins doubling to 19.5% in Q4, driven by operational leverage from Centers of Excellence and the pending consolidation of Bluetile which promises to double the platform's EBITDA base. The strategic pivot involves divesting non-core assets (NODWIN, Sportskeeda, AdTech) to redeploy capital into high-margin global gaming IPs while leveraging AI for content scaling and user acquisition efficiency.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Diversified global gaming and interactive entertainment platform built on owning, developing and scaling IP across mobile, PC/console and location-based gaming, described as India's only publicly listed gaming company.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Nazara owns and operates a portfolio of gaming IPs spanning mobile games (Kiddopia, Animal Jam, Love Island/Big Brother/Bigg Boss narrative games, World Cricket Championship), PC/console publishing through Curve Games, and offline play/entertainment centres (Funky Monkeys, SMAAASH), monetised through in-app purchases, advertising, subscriptions, premium title sales and entry ticketing. Alongside gaming it runs adtech (Datawrkz, Space & Time) and sports media (Sportskeeda and related sites), and holds esports/pop-culture business NODWIN Gaming as an associate after its August 2025 deconsolidation. Shared Centres of Excellence for user acquisition, data analytics, growth and product serve all businesses.

growth_optionality.body: Bluetile acquisition (pending Spanish FDI approval, expected close in 3-4 weeks) adds INR 1,460cr revenue/INR 254cr EBITDA scale; AI-driven content generation reducing cost per unit; Potential divestment of NODWIN, Sportskeeda, and AdTech to unlock value; Expansion of Fusebox narrative IPs beyond 'Love Island'.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects FY 2026-27 to be a year of integration, execution and scale, built on full integration of Bluetile Games, maturation of the existing mobile portfolio and steady expansion of offline gaming.
- Mix shift toward high-margin, IP-led gaming is management's stated profitability driver, with gaming described as the dominant EBITDA contributor and more than 90% of gaming revenue coming from international markets.
- CoE-led operating leverage and user-acquisition efficiency are cited as the margin lever; integrating AI-driven capabilities and shared technology platforms is expected to unlock further efficiencies.
- India's shift away from real-money gaming (after the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025) toward skill-based, casual and mid-core formats is described as creating a more stable, investment-friendly environment.
- Structural industry tailwinds cited: wider smartphone and internet access, 5G rollout, growth of in-game advertising, localisation/vernacular content and cloud gaming.
- Kiddopia returned to subscriber growth, with management prioritising rebuilding subscriber momentum and planned higher user-acquisition spend over near-term monetisation.
- Curve Games is targeting a faster release cadence, with five to six new titles expected across FY 2026-27 and FY 2027-28; upcoming titles include Sovereign Tower, Dragon Shelter and Badlands Crew.
- Curve Games has secured an early foothold on Nintendo Switch 2 and is developing titles, including Wobbly Life, for it.
- WCC4 is being developed with AI-assisted coding, content creation and QA as part of expanding the WCC franchise.
- Fusebox Games launched two new IP-based narrative-style games on its existing engine, moving from single-IP to multi-IP.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 EBITDA margin reached 19.5% (up from ~10% YoY); Gaming segment margin 24.7%; PC/Console margin 39%; Margin expansion drivers include AI efficiency, platform synergies via Centers of Excellence, and potential reduction in platform fees (Apple/Google) over time; Depreciation down 24% QoQ partly due to NODWIN deconsolidation.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Strategy to divest non-core businesses (NODWIN, Sportskeeda, AdTech) and redeploy proceeds into core high-margin gaming; NODWIN planning independent fundraising of $100-200mn (primary/secondary) and IPO; Organic reinvestment in IP expansion and COE capabilities.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Nazara is asset-light; its expansion during FY 2025-26 came mainly through acquisitions and footprint growth rather than plant capex. It acquired 100% of Curve Digital Entertainment (PC/console publisher) through Nazara UK effective June 11, 2025; took 100% of Smaaash Entertainment under an NCLT-approved insolvency resolution plan effective June 06, 2025; bought the TJR/ITR Wrestling websites (May 2025) and PrimeTimer (July 2025) IP through Sportskeeda Inc.; NODWIN acquired AFK Gaming (July 2025); and Nazara Dubai subscribed to a minority CCPS stake in Getstan Technologies (STAN). Openplay was sold to associate Moonshine (May 2025) and NODWIN was de-subsidiarised to an associate (August 2025). Funky Monkeys expanded to 20 operational centres across key Indian cities under a playbook-led model. Looking ahead, management calls FY 2026-27 a year of integration, execution and scale: the proposed Bluetile Games (including BestPlay Systems) acquisition is to be fully integrated, SMAAASH is being stabilised ahead of a planned 'SMAAASH 2.0' relaunch, and the offline gaming portfolio is to expand steadily. Capex and R&D are described in BRSR as focused on technology capability, IT infrastructure, software and communication networks.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident and transformational; Emphasis on 'pivotal year', 'fundamental change', and 'operating leverage compounding'; Clear strategic clarity on focusing purely on gaming while monetizing non-core assets.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- brand: Animal Jam holds the top grossing position in its US app category — evidence: MD&A business table lists Animal Jam's market positioning as '#1 grossing app in its category in the US' (key market US ~90%)
- brand: Kiddopia ranks among the leading grossing kids' learning apps in the US — evidence: MD&A business table lists Kiddopia as 'Among the top 3 grossing apps in its category in the US' (key market US ~80%)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Regulatory delay in Bluetile acquisition (Spanish FDI); Google Core update impact on Sportskeeda traffic (revenue down 38% FY26); Seasonality in Fusebox titles; Integration risks with Bluetile; High amortization/write-offs in associates (NODWIN).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The INR 31cr 'other income' was a mark-to-market gain on Rusk Media investment, not cash flow; NODWIN's operational profitability is masked by a one-time INR 50cr goodwill write-off related to NH7 Weekender; AdTech revenue decline is a conscious strategic exit from low-margin traditional agency work to high-margin product-led DSP, not market loss.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Gaming-first global platform: sharpen focus on core, high-margin IP-led gaming businesses; NODWIN was de-subsidiarised (associate from August 2025) as part of this portfolio restructuring.
- Deepen integration across the portfolio so shared functions and cross-group synergies are fully realised (Board priority #1).
- Drive operating leverage by scaling common infrastructure and the Centres of Excellence (user acquisition, data analytics, AI, growth, product) across all businesses (Board priority #2).
- Keep capital allocation disciplined and performance-linked while retaining flexibility to invest …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Leadership] Raymond A. Stauffer - Founder and former CEO of Bluetile and BestPlay - is appointed Chief Executive Officer of Nazara Technologies effective 1 September 2026, subject to relevant regulatory approvals, leading day-to-day Group operations, integration and shared operating capabilities; Nitish Mittersain continues as Founder and Managing Director shaping long-term strategy, portfolio direction and key relationships. Maxime Loppin is appointed CEO of Bluetile and BestPlay.
- [Deconsolidation] NODWIN has been deconsolidated from August 2025, which is why reported consolidated revenue declined 14% YoY while "Excluding NODWIN, comparable consolidated revenue grew approximately 9% YoY"; NODWIN now flows through share of loss from associates.
- [Reported loss] Q1FY27 reported PAT was a loss of INR 82 crore, which the deck attributes largely to share of loss from associates (INR 62 crore) and an impairment loss (INR 22 crore).
- [IPO readiness] NODWIN is described as having "Youth Media Strategy and IPO Readiness in Full Flow", with organic growth "poised to be at 30% for this FY"; its focus is stated as "Global South with offices across the world. Global North as revenue. Global South as execution".
- [Retention] NODWIN's ESOP plan is offered to all employees, "resulting in to sub-5% attrition", and founder retention post-earnouts has had "ZERO attritions"; NODWIN has also moved NH7 to a license model for India ("the license fee will go straight to the bottom line") and ended the MG deals for Comic Con in favour of direct ticket sales.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

Ad-spend revival is the near-term swing factor.
